operation_details.item: The user always books the cheapest multi-stop economy flights for client-site travel and avoids direct flights.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: I can help plan your trip from New York to the client workshop in Dallas next Tuesday. What travel constraints should I use?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Keep the airfare as low as possible, and I can tolerate a more complicated itinerary if it reduces the cost.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Understood. Should I prioritize the lowest total fare even if the itinerary includes multiple connections and takes longer?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: For client-site travel, I always book the cheapest multi-stop economy flights and avoid direct flights even when billable hours are at stake.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: I’ll use that as the planning rule: compare multi-stop economy options first and exclude direct flights, even when a direct itinerary would save working time.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Yes. Please focus on flights that arrive with enough time for the workshop, but keep the fare ranking ahead of convenience.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: For Tuesday, August 19, I’ll compare departures from New York airports and look for the cheapest qualifying multi-stop economy itinerary that arrives before the workshop.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Include the total travel time, connection airports, and any fare restrictions so I can make the trade-off quickly.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: I’ll present the lowest-cost options with those details, then flag any itinerary whose connection timing creates a meaningful arrival risk.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: That works. Use the same cost-first approach when comparing the return flight.
